newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: SE Asian nations eye new sub-regional grouping.
newsitem.headline: SE Asian nations eye new sub-regional grouping.

text.p: Four Southeast Asian countries are planning to form a sub-regional group which will link industrial and agricultural areas, according to a concept paper released by the Philippines' on Tuesday.

"The establishment of a new growth polygon in the south China Sea region comprising of Central Luzon in the Philippines, Ho Chi Minh in Vietnam, Vientiane in Laos and Phnom Penh in Cambodia is deemed feasible," the concept paper said.
The paper said Vietnam, Cambodia and Laos would have sub-growth centres around their respective capitals.

"This new structure, tagged as regional cross-border cooperation or the growth triangle approach, arises as extensions of the formal trading arrangements only that it affords more ease and convenience in its establishment," it added.

The concept paper did not give specifics, but said the polygon will "promote economic cooperation and development within the growth polygon, accelerate inter- and intra-regional trade and investment activities, and provide an avenue for a strong private sector participation in industrial restructuring and development."
The Philippines and Vietnam are members of the Association of Southeast Asian Nations (ASEAN) which aims to form ASEAN Free Trade Area, an open and free economic region.
Cambodia, Laos and Burma are seeking to become ASEAN members, possibily as early as this year.
Major products produced by Vietnam, Cambodia, and Laos are timber and wood products, while the Philippines could offer construction and professional services, the paper added.
The Board of Investments official said the proposal for the polygon was still in preliminary stages, and China had expressed interest to include its southern provinces in it.
